mainTopic: Can the חכמים uproot a Torah law? (יש כח ביד חכמים לעקור דבר מן התורה). The גמרא finishes deflecting one source and then brings a strong proof from the case of a זר who repays a כהן for eating תרומה.
overview: The גמרא is checking whether the חכמים have the power to uproot a Torah law. First it explains that a woman eating תרומה on her husband's account refers only to תרומה דרבנן. Next it brings a ברייתא about a non-כהן who repaid a כהן with impure חולין. After רבא fills in missing words, it seems that סומכוס in the name of רבי מאיר cancels a payment the Torah considers valid, which would even affect a אשת איש. The גמרא rejects this: 'not payment' only means he must pay a second time. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא shows that the two sides still differ, on fining the accidental payer. Then the גמרא tries the case of impure blood sprinkled on purpose: the ציץ makes it acceptable by Torah law, yet the רבנן say it is not accepted. רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains that only eating the meat is forbidden. When the גמרא objects that this still cancels a Torah מצוה, the answer is that שב ואל תעשה is different.

steps.title: Eating תרומה on his account means תרומה דרבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another line from the source it was examining and explains it as referring only to תרומה דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she eats תרומה because of him.' Answer: this is only תרומה that is rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes one more line from the earlier source and shows it doesn't prove that the חכמים can uproot a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she ate real Torah-level תרומה through a marriage the Torah doesn't recognize, that would show the חכמים overriding Torah law. The גמרא answers that she only eats תרומה דרבנן. Since that תרומה is itself only rabbinic, the חכמים can set its rules, and no Torah law is being uprooted.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of him, on his account
The portion of produce given to a כהן; a non-כהן may not eat it
תרומה required only by rabbinic law, not by the Torah

phrases.english: "And she eats teruma on his account."
With teruma that is rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the previous source by answering its next line.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a rabbinic-level item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating תרומה through a rabbinically valid marriage would mean the חכמים permit a Torah prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers only to תרומה דרבנן, so no Torah law is uprooted.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from this line of the source.

steps.title: A new source: paying back a כהן for eaten תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a non-כהן who ate תרומה and repaid with impure חולין, where סומכוס and the חכמים disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone ate impure תרומה, he pays with pure חולין. If he paid with impure חולין, סומכוס says in the name of רבי מאיר: by accident, his payment counts; on purpose, it doesn't count. The חכמים say: either way his payment counts, and he must pay again with pure חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof attempt by quoting a ברייתא. This step only sets up the source; the actual proof comes in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-כהן who eats תרומה must pay back the כהן with חולין, which then becomes תרומה. The argument is about paying with impure food: סומכוס in the name of רבי מאיר says that if he did it on purpose, the payment is cancelled. That cancellation is what the גמרא will use later.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure
Ordinary, non-sacred food
By accident, unknowingly
On purpose, deliberately
His payment counts as a valid payment

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he ate impure teruma,
phrases.notes: "He" means a non-כהן who ate a כהן's תרומה.

phrases.english: he pays with pure non-sacred food.
If he paid with impure non-sacred food,
Sumakhos says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
If by accident, his payment is a payment;
if on purpose, his payment is not a payment.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה — תַּשְׁלוּמָיו תַּשְׁלוּמִין,
phrases.english: Both this and that, his payment is a payment,
and he goes back and pays again with pure non-sacred food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the last proof was deflected, the גמרא brings a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים can cancel something valid by Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of סומכוס in the name of רבי מאיר about paying with impure חולין

steps.title: Why cancel the payment? He gave the כהן something better
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier question on this ברייתא: paying with impure חולין for impure תרומה is actually a good deal for the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We discussed this: on purpose, his payment doesn't count? He deserves a blessing! He ate something the כהן couldn't use during his days of impurity, and he paid with something the כהן can use during his days of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: Before using the ברייתא, the גמרא recalls a known difficulty with how it reads. Impure תרומה is useless to the כהן, so why would paying with impure חולין be punished?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure תרומה can't be eaten by anyone, so the כהן lost nothing usable. The impure חולין he received can at least be used while the כהן himself is impure. So the ruling that a deliberate payment 'doesn't count' makes no sense for this case.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it: recalls an earlier discussion of this source
Let a blessing come upon him: he deserves praise, not a penalty
Fit, usable
During his days of impurity

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
On purpose, his payment is not a payment?
Let a blessing come upon him!
For he ate from him something
that is not fit for him even during his days of impurity,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the letters in round brackets; the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: and he pays something
that is fit for him during his days of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: בְּמֵזִיד אֵין תַּשְׁלוּמָיו תַּשְׁלוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a difficulty in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that a deliberate payment with impure חולין is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Impure תרומה is useless to the כהן, while impure חולין is usable, so the כהן gained and no penalty makes sense.

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא is missing words
steps.stepSummary: רבא fills in the ברייתא: impure תרומה can be repaid with anything, and the argument is about someone who ate pure תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said (some say it without a name): the ברייתא is missing words, and this is what it teaches. If he ate impure תרומה, he pays with anything. If he ate pure תרומה, he pays with pure חולין. If he paid with impure חולין, סומכוס says in the name of רבי מאיר: by accident it counts, on purpose it doesn't. The חכמים say: either way it counts, and he must pay again with pure חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the difficulty by rebuilding the ברייתא with missing words added in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once words are added, the argument is about someone who ate pure תרומה, which the כהן really could have eaten. Paying him back with impure food on purpose cheats the כהן. That is why רבי מאיר cancels the payment. For impure תרומה, any payment is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Without a name: the statement is said with no specific author
It is missing words: the text is incomplete
Anything at all
Ritually pure

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the case is still impure תרומה. After רבא's fix, the argument between סומכוס and the חכמים is about someone who ate PURE תרומה and repaid with impure חולין.

phrases.english: And Rava said, and some say it without attribution:
The baraita is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל תְּרוּמָה טְמֵאָה — מְשַׁלֵּם כָּל דְּהוּ.
phrases.english: If he ate impure teruma, he pays with anything.

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל תְּרוּמָה טְהוֹרָה — מְשַׁלֵּם חוּלִּין טְהוֹרִין,
phrases.english: If he ate pure teruma, he pays with pure non-sacred food;
if he paid with impure non-sacred food,
Sumakhos says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
If by accident, his payment is a payment;
if on purpose, his payment is not a payment.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּשׁוֹגֵג בֵּין בְּמֵזִיד — תַּשְׁלוּמָיו תַּשְׁלוּמִין,
phrases.english: Whether by accident or on purpose, his payment is a payment,
and he goes back and pays again with pure non-sacred food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מיחסרא: adding missing words to the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about repaying impure תרומה, where cancelling the payment makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about repaying pure תרומה with impure חולין, where the כהן is shortchanged.

steps.title: The proof: the חכמים cancel a payment the Torah considers valid
steps.stepSummary: By Torah law the impure חולין is a real payment that even works for קידושין, yet the חכמים cancel it. In effect, they treat a truly married woman as unmarried.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, by Torah law it is a proper payment, so much so that if a כהן betroths a woman with it, the קידושין takes effect. Yet the חכמים said his payment is not a payment, and so we release a married woman to everyone!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא draws the proof it set up in step 2. The חכמים can cancel something the Torah treats as fully valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law the food belongs to the כהן, so he could use it to betroth a woman. If the חכמים say the payment is void, the food is not his, and the קידושין fails. That means a woman who is married by Torah law would be allowed to marry anyone, showing the חכמים uprooting a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
Proper, fully valid
Betroths (performs קידושין)
The קידושין takes effect on her
A married woman

steps.whatToRemember: This proof says that, according to סומכוס in the name of רבי מאיר, the חכמים cancel a payment that is valid by Torah law, even though this would affect a אשת איש. The next steps (6-8) reject it: the first payment stays valid, and he only has to pay a second time.
steps.whyThisMatters: This proof attempt in the סוגיא of יש כח ביד חכמים לעקור דבר מן התורה reaches as far as marriage, the most serious area. That is why the גמרא works hard in the next steps (6-8) to deflect it.

phrases.english: And here,
by Torah law it is a proper payment,
for if a priest betroths a woman with them,
the betrothal takes effect on her,
and the Sages said his payment is not a payment,
phrases.notes: This is the view of סומכוס in the name of רבי מאיר for someone who paid on purpose.

phrases.english: and so we release a married woman to everyone!
phrases.notes: Literally "we permit" her: she would be treated as unmarried and free to marry anyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא, דְּמִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא תַּשְׁלוּמֵי מְעַלְּיָא הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the ברייתא now clarified, the גמרא draws its proof from it.
steps.raayaObject: יש כח ביד חכמים לעקור דבר מן התורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: סומכוס in the name of רבי מאיר: a deliberate payment with impure חולין is void, even though by Torah law it is valid enough for קידושין

steps.title: The first payment still counts; he just pays again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. 'His payment is not payment' does not cancel the first payment. It only means he must also pay again with pure חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does רבי מאיר mean by 'his payment is not payment'? He means the person has to go back and pay again with pure חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 5 by reading the phrase 'his payment is not payment' in a softer way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 assumed the חכמים cancel a payment that is valid by Torah law. Here the גמרא says the impure חולין he already gave stays a real payment and belongs to the כהן. The חכמים only add a second payment of pure חולין, so nothing the Torah validated is actually cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: payment; here, repaying the כהן for תרומה that was eaten
to go back, to do again
ritually pure non-holy food

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not payment' does not mean the first payment is thrown out. It stays with the כהן as תרומה. The person simply owes a second, proper payment.

phrases.english: What is 'his payment is not payment'
that רבי מאיר said?
phrases.notes: This is the opinion in the ברייתא from step 2 that סומכוס quoted in רבי מאיר's name.

phrases.english: That he needs to go back
and pay with pure חולין.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֵין תַּשְׁלוּמָיו תַּשְׁלוּמִין דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof drawn in step 5 by reinterpreting the key phrase.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the חכמים cancel a Torah-valid payment.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'not payment' cancels the first payment. Really it only requires an extra payment, and the first one stays valid.

steps.title: Then סומכוס and the רבנן agree
steps.stepSummary: If the first payment counts and he pays again, that is exactly what the רבנן say. So what are סומכוס and the רבנן arguing about?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, סומכוס is saying the same thing as the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from step 6, because it seems to erase the argument in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן in the ברייתא hold that the payment counts and he still pays again with pure חולין. If רבי מאיר's 'not payment' (as quoted by סומכוס) means the same thing, the two opinions look identical. A ברייתא would not record a disagreement where there is none.

keyTerms.meaning: if so; if what you just said is true
that is the same as

phrases.english: If so,
סומכוס is the same as the רבנן!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reinterpretation given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'his payment is not payment' as only requiring a second payment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes the two sides of the ברייתא say the same thing, which leaves them no disagreement.

steps.title: The difference is fining the accidental sinner
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא says they differ on whether the חכמים fined someone who acted by accident because of someone who acted on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא said: the difference between them is whether the חכמים fined the accidental sinner because of the deliberate one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא answers the challenge by showing a real difference between סומכוס and the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס, quoting רבי מאיר, requires a second payment only from someone who acted on purpose. If he acted by accident, his payment is enough. The רבנן make even the accidental payer pay again, so that people will not take the rule lightly when acting on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: they fined; the חכמים imposed a penalty
someone who acted by mistake
someone who acted on purpose
because of; for fear of
there is a difference between them

steps.whyThisMatters: Either way, the first payment stays valid. So the case of repaying with impure חולין no longer proves that the חכמים cancel a Torah-valid act.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: רב אחא son of רב איקא said:
'They fined the accidental one because of the deliberate one'
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא: קָנְסוּ שׁוֹגֵג אַטּוּ מֵזִיד אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference between the two opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the first payment counts for both sides, they seem to say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ on whether the accidental payer must also pay again. סומכוס says no, and the רבנן say yes.

steps.title: A new source: impure blood sprinkled on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new source. If a כהן sprinkled impure blood by accident, the offering is accepted. If he did it on purpose, it is not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: blood that became impure and the כהן sprinkled it. If by accident, the offering is accepted. If on purpose, it is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a fresh proof that the חכמים can override a Torah law. This step only presents the case; the next step explains why it is a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on whether the כהן acted by accident or on purpose. The גמרא will now show that by Torah law both cases should be accepted. So the 'not accepted' ruling for the deliberate case must come from the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: he sprinkled it (the blood on the מזבח)
it was accepted; the offering works

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Blood that became impure, and he sprinkled it,
if by accident, it is accepted;
if on purpose, it is not accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from repaying with impure חולין fell away, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים can override what the Torah treats as valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching about impure blood sprinkled on the מזבח.

steps.title: The ציץ makes it acceptable, yet the רבנן reject it
steps.stepSummary: By Torah law the ציץ makes impure blood acceptable even when sprinkled on purpose. Still, the רבנן say it is not accepted, so the owner brings a new animal. By Torah law that animal is חולין, and he is bringing it into the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, by Torah law it is accepted. As a ברייתא teaches: What does the ציץ make acceptable? Blood, meat and fat that became impure, whether by accident or on purpose, whether forced or willingly, whether for a private offering or a communal one. Yet the רבנן say it is not accepted, and so he ends up bringing חולין into the עזרה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the impure blood case is a proof. The Torah accepts the offering, but the חכמים reject it, and their ruling leads to a real Torah problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that the ציץ works 'whether by accident or on purpose,' so by Torah law the owner has already fulfilled his obligation. Because the רבנן say 'not accepted,' he must bring another animal, which by Torah law is not a real offering. So the חכמים are causing him to bring חולין into the עזרה, a Torah prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: the gold plate worn on the כהן גדול's forehead
makes an offering acceptable
by Torah law
bringing non-holy animals into the Temple courtyard, which the Torah forbids
something forced or unavoidable

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from repaying with impure חולין fell away, because the first payment still counts. The new proof is the impure blood case. By Torah law the ציץ makes the offering acceptable even when done on purpose. Still, the רבנן reject it, which leads the owner to bring חולין into the עזרה.

phrases.english: But here, by Torah law it really is accepted,
as a ברייתא teaches: For what does the ציץ make acceptable?
For the blood, and for the meat,
and for the fat that became impure,
whether by accident or on purpose,
whether forced or willingly,
whether for an individual or for the community.
And the רבנן say: it is not accepted,
phrases.notes: This means when the כהן sprinkled on purpose, as in step 9.

phrases.english: and so he ends up bringing חולין into the עזרה!
phrases.notes: Since the Torah already counted the first offering, the new animal he brings is really just חולין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof started in step 9 by showing the Torah law contradicts the רבנן's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים can override a Torah law, even to the point of causing an action the Torah forbids.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that the ציץ makes impure offerings acceptable even when done on purpose, together with the רבנן's ruling that a deliberate sprinkling is not accepted.

steps.title: Rereading 'Not Accepted': Only the Meat Is Forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains that 'not accepted' in the ברייתא only forbids eating the meat. The בעלים still get their כפרה, so no new animal is needed and no חולין is brought into the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: What does the ברייתא mean when it says 'it is not accepted'? It is not accepted to allow the meat to be eaten. But the owners did get atonement through it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא pushes back on the proof from step 10 by giving a narrower reading of the words 'not accepted.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 10 assumed that 'not accepted' means the owner must bring a new animal, which would be חולין brought into the עזרה. רבי יוסי בר חנינא says the penalty only forbids eating the meat. The owner's כפרה is complete, so no new animal is brought, and the proof that the רבנן force an active wrong falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Was accepted. Said of a קרבן that 'worked' properly.
The owners of the קרבן, the people who brought it.
They received atonement (כפרה).
Eating. Here it means the כהנים eating the meat of the קרבן.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not accepted' here does NOT mean the קרבן failed completely. It failed only for eating the meat. The atonement still worked.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
What is the meaning of 'it is not accepted' that it says?
phrases.notes: He's quoting the ברייתא from step 9 about blood sprinkled on purpose.

phrases.english: It is not accepted to permit the meat to be eaten,
but the owners have gained atonement through it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 10 by narrowing what 'not accepted' means.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the owner must bring a new animal, which would mean the רבנן force him to bring חולין into the עזרה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof read 'not accepted' as a total failure. It really only means the meat may not be eaten, and the כפרה stands.

steps.title: But Forbidding the Meat Still Cancels a Torah מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: even on this reading, the Torah מצוה of eating the meat is uprooted. The פסוק teaches that the כהנים eat the meat and through that the owners get כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, the eating of the meat is still being uprooted. And the Torah says: 'And they shall eat those things through which atonement was made.' This teaches that the כהנים eat and the owners get atonement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי בר חנינא: his new reading still has the רבנן cancelling a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if no new animal is brought, the רבנן forbid the meat. But the פסוק makes eating the meat a Torah מצוה, tied to the owners' כפרה. So we still have the רבנן overriding Torah law, and the question remains.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end; either way. Used to say the problem has not gone away.
Is uprooted; is cancelled.
Atonement was made.
It teaches. Introduces the lesson learned from a פסוק.

phrases.english: Ultimately, the eating of the meat is being uprooted,
and it is written: 'And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made,'
this teaches that the priests eat

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוסי בר חנינא's reading by showing it still has the רבנן overriding a Torah law.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי בר חנינא's claim that only the eating of the meat is affected.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating the meat is itself a Torah מצוה, based on the פסוק in שמות. So forbidding it still means the רבנן uproot Torah law.

steps.title: Doing Nothing Is Different
steps.stepSummary: The answer: when the חכמים uproot a Torah law by telling us to sit and not act (שב ואל תעשה), that is allowed. It is different from telling us to actively do something.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Sit and do not act' is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Forbidding the meat only makes the כהנים hold back from eating, and the חכמים are allowed to do that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of rabbinic rules. One tells you to actively do something against the Torah, like bringing חולין into the עזרה. The other only tells you to hold back from doing a מצוה, which is called שב ואל תעשה. Forbidding the meat is the second kind, so it does not prove that the רבנן can require an active wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Sit and do not act.' A ruling that tells you to stay passive and not do something.
Is different.

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים can uproot a Torah law by telling us to do nothing (שב ואל תעשה). That does not prove they can make us actively do something against the Torah. So 'not accepted' only forbids the meat, the owners keep their כפרה, and no חולין is brought into the עזרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of שב ואל תעשה is a key principle used throughout ש״ס. It explains when rabbinic rules may override a Torah מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה שָׁאנֵי.
phrases.english: He said to him: 'sit and do not act' is different.
phrases.notes: He means: holding back from eating is passive, unlike actively bringing an animal into the עזרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 by separating passive rules from active ones.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between categories: passive refraining versus active doing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any rabbinic rule that cancels a Torah מצוה, even just forbidding the meat, shows the רבנן override the Torah the same way as forcing an action.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים may uproot a Torah law through שב ואל תעשה. Forbidding the meat is only that, so the case does not show them requiring an active wrong.
